title: A century becomes a mechanism
text: Before a watch could follow us around the Earth, it had to survive the world. In 1926, Rolex created the Oyster: a sealed refuge for a tiny mechanical heart. In 1931, the Perpetual rotor began turning the wearer's movement into stored energy. Then, in 1955, the GMT-Master gave travellers a second horizon: two time zones on one wrist. In 2012, the Sky-Dweller carried that story further. Beneath white gold, calibre 9001 brought two time zones together with an annual calendar called Saros. Its name evokes the great eighteen-year cycle of eclipses. Here, the celestial dance becomes machinery: a fixed wheel, an orbiting satellite, four fingers that recognise the thirty-day months. Come closer. Watch a year take shape, one extraordinary midnight at a time.
